name: HubSpot

identity.note: HubSpot CRM platform (Marketing, Sales, Service, Content hubs). API endpoints are date-versioned (e.g. 2026-03, 2026-09).

summary: HubSpot is a CRM and marketing, sales and service platform with a broad REST API for CRM objects and more.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 is required for apps distributed to multiple accounts (marketplace, or private distribution capped at 10 allowlisted accounts). A static auth access token from the app settings works for a single account. Legacy API keys are retired.

gates: Marketplace-listed OAuth apps need HubSpot app review; unlisted 'private' distribution is limited to 10 allowlisted accounts
Some APIs and endpoints depend on the customer's hub and subscription tier, and rate limits differ by tier
Developer test accounts expire after 90 days without API calls unless renewed

api.note: Base URL is https://api.hubapi.com with date-based versioning; each version stays supported until its end-of-life date. Rate limits vary by subscription tier. I did not read the API-by-tier table directly.

mcp.note: HubSpot hosts a remote MCP server for CRM records, with OAuth sign-in handled by the AI tool. It also offers a local Developer MCP server for app and CMS development.

open_questions: Exact per-tier rate limits and which endpoints need Professional or Enterprise were not read in detail (see the 'APIs by tier' page).
Marketplace listing review requirements and timelines were not checked.

claims.text: OAuth is required for apps distributed to multiple accounts; static auth tokens are for a single account.
claims.quote: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while static auth access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.

claims.text: Private OAuth distribution is capped at 10 accounts; marketplace distribution makes the app eligible for listing.
claims.quote: If you choose this option, you can install your app in a maximum of 10 accounts at a time.

claims.text: Developer test accounts are free, up to 10 per account, with a 90-day trial of enterprise features.
claims.quote: Developer test accounts are free HubSpot accounts with access to a 90-day trial of many enterprise features, with the following limitations:

claims.text: REST API at api.hubapi.com with date-based versioning, covering CRM objects such as contacts.
claims.quote: All APIs, whether legacy, new, or beta, use the same root path as before: `https://api.hubapi.com/`.

claims.text: HubSpot publishes an official hosted remote MCP server for CRM data.
claims.quote: It enables an agent to read, write, and update HubSpot records (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and more) as a user would.

name: Close

identity.note: Close (close.com) CRM for sales teams, formerly Close.io.

summary: Close is a sales CRM with built-in calling, email, SMS, pipelines and automation for managing leads, contacts and opportunities.

auth.detail: API key via HTTP Basic Auth (key as username, empty password) for single-org use. OAuth 2.0 authorization code for multi-customer apps; register an OAuth app in Settings > Developer to get Client ID/Secret. All OAuth apps get all.full_access offline_access scopes.

gates: Developer needs a Close account; 14-day free trial, no credit card required
OAuth apps are Private by default (only members of your own Close org can authorize); a Public app must be submitted for review before any Close customer can authorize it
Integrations Directory listing requires OAuth and an email to support@close.com
Some endpoints/features are plan-dependent (custom objects, Scale only; custom activities, Growth and Scale; workflows, Growth and up)
The pricing page says Growth plan includes no daily API request quota, implying lower tiers have one

api.note: REST/JSON, offset or cursor pagination, rate limits with 429 and exponential backoff. SDKs are community-built (Python, PHP, Node, Ruby, Go, C#). Event log keeps 30 days.

mcp.note: Vendor-hosted remote MCP at developer.close.com/mcp: HTTP Streamable, OAuth 2.0 with Dynamic Client Registration, or API key headers. Tool scopes: mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive.

open_questions: Exact daily API quota on Solo/Essentials plans was not verified.
Whether the free trial gives full API access was not stated explicitly, though the API docs show no plan restriction.

claims.text: Close supports API keys (HTTP Basic) and OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: Use HTTP Basic Auth with your API key as the username and an empty password.

claims.text: OAuth apps are registered in Close to get client credentials, with full-access scopes.
claims.quote: All OAuth applications are granted the `all.full_access offline_access` scopes, providing the same level of access as API keys.

claims.text: Public OAuth apps need Close review; private apps only work within the developer's own org.
claims.quote: OAuth apps are **Private** by default, meaning only members of your own Close organization can authorize them.

claims.text: 14-day free trial with no credit card.
Growth plan advertises no daily API request quota, implying a quota on lower tiers.
claims.quote: Build integrations that scale No daily API request quota or per-request fees.

claims.text: Broad REST API across CRM objects, activities, webhooks, sequences and reporting.
claims.quote: Leads are the most important object in Close.

claims.text: Webhook subscriptions are supported for real-time events.
claims.quote: Configure webhook subscriptions to receive real-time event notifications from Close.

claims.text: Close publishes an official remote MCP server with OAuth DCR.
claims.quote: The MCP server URL is `https://mcp.close.com/mcp` and has “HTTP Streamable” and “OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)” support.
